text:
maria: Heads up — eu-west1c just had a noisy burst of tiny-gang pod evictions starting ~09:12. I’m seeing ~30 evictions across multiple racks, lots of tiny-pod churn. Anyone on call? :grimacing:

ops-bot: ALERT eu-west1c: node-network-flap detected on rack-r5-12, auto-eviction policy applied to best-effort pods.

kevin: on it, pulling scheduler traces. Did we get any recent warm-pool or provisioning changes?

maria: not from us. No recent rollouts. Attaching a sample kubectl describe from one of the evicted pods: 

```
Name:         tiny-worker-7f4c9
Namespace:    ml-jobs
Node:         ip-10-3-24-98.eu-west1c/10.3.24.98
Start Time:   Tue, 14 Mar 2026 09:05:47 +0000
Status:       Failed
Reason:       Evicted
Message:      The node was low on resource: NodeNotReady. Kubelet evicted pods to recover.
Events:
  Type     Reason        Age   From               Message
  ----     ------        ----  ----               -------
  Warning  Evicted       8m    kubelet, ip-10-3-24-98  Pod eviction triggered by node not ready (network plugin reported NIC down)
```

jess: that looks like a node-network failure causing kubelet to mark NotReady and then standard eviction window. But 30 evictions in 10m is high — seems like a ripple where gang-scheduled tiny pods got redistributed and preempted each other.

sam: could be placement churn + affinity constraints. If scheduler backs off and requeues many tiny-gang pods simultaneously, they compete for the same scarce NVidia slots and cause cascading preemptions.

kevin: I’m looking at scheduler metrics — saw a spike in scheduling attempts and binder retries at 09:11:50. BindLatency P50 jumped from 30ms -> 450ms for tiny-gang class. Also descheduler didn’t run for 6h.

li: paging networking team — ToR in rack-r5 shows flapping at 09:10-09:15, ecounters indicate brief interface resets. I’ve opened INC-12345 with infra-net. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-12345

jess: short-term mitigations? We should avoid draining more nodes. Options: 1) temporarily cordon affected rack nodes with a custom taint to stop new scheduling there, 2) scale up warm-pool capacity in eu-west1c to absorb reschedules, 3) run a targeted descheduler to coalesce scattered tiny pods onto fewer nodes so they don’t keep displacing each other.

sam: +1 for cordon/taint on the specific rack (maintenance=network:NoSchedule) to halt immediate churn while infra works the switch. But be cautious: cordoning can trigger reschedules elsewhere and make other racks noisy.

maria: I can apply a taint to the five affected nodes and add a temporary placement-rule to critical jobs. Will wait for a thumbs from eng-sre.

kevin: I’ll kick a descheduler job with these flags: `--policy-file=/etc/descheduler/policy-coalesce.json --evict-local-storage=false --ignore-daemonsets=true` to try to pack tiny pods.

li: infra-net responded — switch reboot scheduled, ETA 20m. They recommend keeping new scheduling off that rack until reboot completes.

deploy-bot: Note: no user-facing deploys in the last 30m.

jess: After the taint + descheduler + switch reboot, monitor tokenized eviction rate and binder latency. If eviction rate > 5/min for 10m we escalate to full warm-pool scale-up.

maria: I applied `maintenance=network:NoSchedule` to rack-r5 nodes and added a prometheus alert for `evictions_total{zone="eu-west1c"}` > 5/min. Kicked the descheduler.

kevin: scheduler traces show bind retries dropping back to baseline after ~7m. Evictions tapering. Nice job.

li: infra-net confirms switch rebooted, ToR appears stable. They’ll run checks for flapping ASIC ports.

sam: follow-up items: (1) add a preempt-throttle for tiny-gang class so we don't cascade on transient node failures, (2) enable periodic descheduler cadence for tiny pods, (3) evaluate affinity rules that push tiny gangs to spread too aggressively.

maria: filing a short blameless follow-up doc with lessons + action items. Tagging @kevin @jess @li for next-steps. Thanks everyone. :pray:
